## Setup

Since each hemisphere satisfies $D^n_\pm / \partial D^n_\pm \cong S^n$, and the two quotients share the collapsed point, we have a canonical homeomorphism $S^n / S^{n-1} \cong S^n \vee S^n$. Denote the two wedge summands by $S^n_1$ and $S^n_2$.

## The cofiber sequence and long exact sequence

The inclusion $i: S^{n-1} \hookrightarrow S^n$ of the equator has cofiber $S^n \vee S^n$, giving the cofiber sequence
$$S^{n-1} \xrightarrow{i} S^n \xrightarrow{q} S^n \vee S^n \xrightarrow{\delta} \Sigma S^{n-1} = S^n \to \cdots$$

The associated long exact sequence in reduced homology (for $n \geq 2$) is:
$$\cdots \to \widetilde{H}_n(S^{n-1})=0 \to \widetilde{H}_n(S^n)\cong\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{q_*} \widetilde{H}_n(S^n\vee S^n)\cong\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{\partial} \widetilde{H}_{n-1}(S^{n-1})\cong\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{i_*} \widetilde{H}_{n-1}(S^n)=0 \to \cdots$$

## Computing $q_*$ on $H_n$

Since $\widetilde{H}_n(S^{n-1})=0$, the map $q_*:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}$ is **injective**. Since $\widetilde{H}_{n-1}(S^n)=0$, the map $i_*$ is zero, so the connecting homomorphism $\partial:\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is **surjective**. By exactness, $\operatorname{im}(q_*)=\ker(\partial)$.

Under the identification $H_n(S^n\vee S^n)\cong H_n(S^n,S^{n-1})$ (via the quotient isomorphism), the class $[S^n_1]$ corresponds to the relative fundamental class $[D^n_+,\partial D^n_+]$ and $[S^n_2]$ to $[D^n_-,\partial D^n_-]$.

The connecting homomorphism $\partial$ sends a relative class to the homology class of its boundary:
- $\partial([D^n_+,\partial D^n_+]) = [\partial D^n_+] = [S^{n-1}]$ (the fundamental class of the equator with its **outward** orientation from $D^n_+$).
- $\partial([D^n_-,\partial D^n_-]) = [\partial D^n_-] = -[S^{n-1}]$ (the boundary orientation from $D^n_-$ is **opposite**, since the two hemispheres induce opposite orientations on the shared equator).

Therefore $\partial(a,b) = a - b$, and:
$$\ker(\partial) = \{(a,a): a\in\mathbb{Z}\} = \langle(1,1)\rangle$$

Since $\operatorname{im}(q_*)=\ker(\partial)$ and $q_*$ is injective with $\mathbb{Z}$ as domain:
$$\boxed{q_*([S^n]) = [S^n_1]+[S^n_2], \quad\text{i.e., } q_*(1)=(1,1)}$$

This is the **diagonal map** $\Delta: \mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}$.

**Direct verification:** The fundamental class $[S^n]$ decomposes as $[D^n_+,\partial D^n_+] + [D^n_-,\partial D^n_-]$ in $H_n(S^n, S^{n-1})$ (the fundamental class of a closed oriented manifold is the sum of the relative fundamental classes of its halves). Under $q$, each relative class maps to the absolute fundamental class of the corresponding wedge summand. Hence $q_*([S^n]) = [S^n_1]+[S^n_2]$, confirming the result.

For $n \geq 2$: $H_{n-1}(S^n) = 0$ (the sphere has homology only in degrees $0$ and $n$) and $H_{n-1}(S^n\vee S^n)=0$ (the wedge of two $n$-spheres also has homology only in degrees $0$ and $n$). Therefore:
$$q_*: H_{n-1}(S^n) \to H_{n-1}(S^n\vee S^n) \quad\text{is the zero map } 0\to 0.$$

This is consistent with the long exact sequence: the segment $\widetilde{H}_{n-1}(S^{n-1})\cong\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{i_*} \widetilde{H}_{n-1}(S^n)=0 \xrightarrow{q_*} \widetilde{H}_{n-1}(S^n\vee S^n)=0$ shows $q_*$ is the zero map on $H_{n-1}$, with the non-trivial content of the sequence residing in the **connecting homomorphism** $\partial:\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ given by $(a,b)\mapsto a-b$, which is the map at the $(n-1)$-th level that carries the essential topological information.

For $n=1$: $H_0(S^1)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ and $H_0(S^1\vee S^1)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ (both connected), and $q_*$ is the identity $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.

The map $q:S^n\to S^n\vee S^n$ collapsing the equator induces:

| Homology | Map |
|---|---|
| $H_n$ ($n\geq 1$) | $q_*(1)=(1,1)$ — the **diagonal** $\mathbb{Z}\xrightarrow{\Delta}\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}$ |
| $H_{n-1}$ ($n\geq 2$) | $q_*=0$ — the zero map $0\to 0$ |
| $H_0$ ($n=1$) | $q_*=\mathrm{id}$ — the identity $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ |

The connecting homomorphism at the $(n-1)$-th level is $\partial(a,b)=a-b$, and the exactness relation $\operatorname{im}(q_*)=\ker(\partial)$ at the $H_n$ level ties the diagonal map to the difference map, completing the exact sequence.
